To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have cloned five rat trp-related genes, (2) we have cloned two cDNAs homologous to the trp gene from Drosphila photoreceptor, and (3) we have shown that the expression of rat TRP genes in COS cells increases the CCE.
the TRP channel is a key molecule in CCE, and that TRP channels are expressed in brain.
we have identified five different rat TRP homologues and characterized two of them, rTRP3 and rTRP6, which are differentially expressed in brain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cloning and expression of rat trp homology in the brain.
the cloning and characterization of the TRP channel gene family, which is a candidate for the SOC.
the cloning and expression of rat TRP genes and their possible involvement in CCE.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
TRP3 and/or TRP6 may be involved in CCE or SOC.
the TRP gene family, which includes TRP1-TRP6, is the most likely candidate for the molecular identity of the CCE or SOC channel.
the TRP family of ion channels are expressed in a variety of tissues in a cell type- and tissue-specific manner and are involved in various cellular functions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TRP3 and/or TRP6 are involved in the CCE in the brain.
TRP channels are involved in the regulation of intracellular calcium concentration and may be important for the modulation of synaptic transmission in the brain.
TRP channels are a family of ion channel proteins that are expressed in a wide variety of cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
TRP3 and 6 can function as CCE in rat brain.
we found five rat trp genes and cloned two of them.
TRP6 is expressed at higher levels than TRP3 and that TRP6, but not TRP3, is localized to the hippocampus and cortex.
